reaction: The landscape connection was satisfying and matched my expectation.

expectation: The inspection will show which available objects can interact with the grassland.

effect: Grassland had one available partner, and the automatic combination produced grazing herds.
reaction: That clarified the first link in the food web.
reason: The herds need something that eats them; small furred animals might provide a predator lineage, though this is a guess.
expectation: This may produce predators or a feeding relationship.

effect: Small furred animals were not the herds' partner; the herds can instead combine with grassland or water.
reaction: The feedback makes the next step clearer, though the predator guess was wrong.
reason: Combining grazers with their grassland is a plausible way to establish their feeding relationship.
expectation: The herds will feed on the grassland, creating a link in the food web.

alternatives.reason: Water is also a known partner, but seems less directly related to feeding.

effect: Grazing herds and grassland produced dung, suggesting a route through waste and nutrient recycling.
reaction: The result makes the less obvious waste link concrete.
reason: Dung returning to soil is a plausible next step toward connecting waste with new growth.
expectation: The dung may enrich the soil or begin a decomposition pathway.

alternatives.reason: Its partners could clarify how the waste is recycled.

reaction: The beetles make the waste link more interesting and concrete.
reason: Dung beetles may connect their use of dung to the soil and nutrient recycling.
expectation: The beetles may return nutrients to the soil or otherwise help new growth.

alternatives.reason: Checking their partners would clarify their role, but the soil connection seems plausible.

effect: Dung beetles and soil produced fertile grassland, connecting animal waste to renewed growth.
reaction: That completes a satisfying nutrient-recycling link.
reason: The fertile grassland may connect back to the grazing herds and complete the feeding cycle.
expectation: The herds may feed on the renewed grassland, completing a food-web link.

reaction: The sensory link to feeding was unexpected but clear.

expectation: This may create a predator or a predator-prey relationship.

expectation: The inspection will show available partners for connecting the predator-prey relationship to the wider community.

effect: Predator and prey combined automatically with fertile grassland to make a food web, connecting the hunting and nutrient-recycling branches and completing the goal.
reaction: The converging branches were satisfying, and the reminder that relationships can change was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making dung beetles and fertile grassland made the path from waste to renewed growth concrete; joining it to predator and prey showed how the branches overlap.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to combine fertile grassland back with the herds was a dead end; I expected a visible return link, but it had no available combinations.

surprise.text: Scent tracking emerged from small mammals and air before it became part of hunting mammals. That sensory step was unexpected but understandable.

arbitrary.text: The initial pairing of shore plants and rain shadow to make grassland was a plausible guess, but the transformation itself gave little explanation of how that habitat arose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more branches converge: the food web made the world feel connected without presenting its inhabitants as pieces placed merely to balance a design.
